*   **School z:** I have priority 2. In the worst case, everyone else also ranks z highly, and there is at least one other student with priority 1 at z. In this case, I will be rejected by z.

*   **School w:** I have priority 1. Similar to school y, I am guaranteed to be matched with w if I rank it, since my priority is 1.

*   **School x:** I have priority 2. In the worst case, everyone else also ranks x highly, and there is at least one other student with priority 1 at x. In this case, I will be rejected by x.

Considering the worst-case scenarios, I am guaranteed to be matched with either y or w if I rank them. Since my preference is y > z > w > x, I should rank y first. If I get rejected from y (which is impossible since I have priority 1), I would like to be matched with z. If I am rejected from z, I would like to be matched with w. Finally, x is my least preferred.

Therefore, my ranking should be y > z > w > x.
